used_notes: Yes. Raw notes were essential. Aggregated statistics alone would misrank candidates that appeared strong (multi-region, multi-site) but had events out of causal order or single-source critical links. Notes revealed that C-1, C-5, and C-37 lack genuine causal progression despite good aggregate numbers; the regional/site counts masked broken chains and weak independent reporting on key events.
reasoning_notes: Ranked by: (1) matching 7 known causal chains with events in temporal order; (2) cross-organizational spread (3+ regions, 4+ sites preferred); (3) independent sourcing (3+ sources/event ideal); (4) temporal progression (events spread 30+ days); (5) penalties for contradictions and single-day events. Real risks (17 candidates) have 4-5+ linked events from known chains, multi-region/multi-site independent reports, and progression over weeks-to-months. Top: C-12 (auth->api->checkout->revenue via cert rotation), C-39 (supply chain from component defect), C-6 (full policy->audit->regulatory chain). Bottom-ranked are broken chains, single-source final events, or scattered events from unrelated chains.
